sentence: This project studies eukaryotic pathogens that cause disease, using molecular, cellular, genetic and genomic approaches.
This project tries to find out how a metabolite builds up in aggressive gliomas and how it affects interactions between glioma cells and neurons.
This project builds nanoparticles that boost antigen presentation and T cell responses, and tests them against cancer in mouse models.
This project studies how hepatitis C virus spreads from cell to cell, using molecular virology and mathematical modeling.
This project builds a modeling framework that combines mechanistic models and graph neural networks to predict how childhood infections spread among connected populations.
This project studies the genetic, neuroimaging and behavioral factors that come before an eating disorder starts in adolescence.
This project studies how DNA hypermethylation and 3D genome architecture are linked in acute myeloid leukemia samples and cell line models.
This project combines artificial intelligence and perfusion imaging to build a biomarker for personalized dosimetry in radioembolization of liver cancer.
This project studies how weather affects viral shedding in bats and the risk of spillover of zoonotic infections.
This project coordinates work on adeno-associated virus gene therapy and base editing for alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency.
This project supports an Alzheimer's disease research project that looks for biological pathways that protect against Alzheimer's disease.
This project tries to find out which bioactive peptides are released from human milk proteins in the gut of preterm infants.
This project uses computational methods to study how mutation, natural selection and genetic drift have shaped human genomes and gene expression.
This project provides computational analysis of high throughput data to help study basic mechanisms of cancers, including melanoma, prostate and lung cancer.
This project builds an X-ray source that gives monochromatic energies for mammography and tests it in a clinical trial.
This project studies how astrocytes in glioblastoma suppress immune responses, using mouse models and clinical data.
This project studies the mechanisms behind sensory neuropathy linked to HIV infection.
This project studies brain circuits affected early in Alzheimer's disease, using mouse models and samples from human patients.
This project applies complex imaging methods to understand the neuroscience of misuse and dependence of cocaine, opiate, nicotine and alcohol.
This project studies how a motor protein moves cargo in kidney cells and how losing it causes kidney disease in mice.
